newsitem.title: USA: AMR, pilots back at table, with new airline offer.
newsitem.headline: AMR, pilots back at table, with new airline offer.

text.p: American Airlines and its pilots resumed contract talks Wednesday with a new proposal from the carrier on the table.
An American Air official said the new proposal increased the carrier's pay offer to a six percent pay raise over four years, up from five percent previously.
The Allied Pilots Association has asked for 11.5 percent.
The American Air official said the new proposal also drops one of two stock options offered to the pilots, but retains the other, at a $10 discount.
The official said the offer was designed to meet an apparent goal of the pilots -- additional wages rather than later income through stock -- but would allow American Air to remain competitive.
There was no immediate response from the pilots union.
The pilots are threatening to strike the airline at midnight Friday.
American Air is a unit of AMR Corp.
A federal mediator said at a bargaining break on Tuesday that he remained hopeful a settlement could be reached to avert a strike at the No. 2 U.S. carrier.
A strike would disrupt travel for the 200,000 passengers the carrier flies on its 2,200 routes worldwide every day.
The two sides reached a tentative accord last September, but the pilots' rank-and-file rejected it in December, leading to the strike deadline and the federally-mediated bagaining.

Pilots union president James Sovich said the union's board of directors would be on hand in Washigton today -- one day sooner than previously scheduled. Board action is needed for approval of any settlement.
Aside from pay, also at issue is American Air's plan for its regional carrier, American Eagle, to use jets flown by lower-paid members of another union.

American Air has said it needs the jets flown by lower-paid pilots to remain competitive with other major U.S. carriers who are increasingly dropping turboprop craft for small jets on commuter services.
